svg.title: Why IPsec breaks large packets: the encapsulation arithmetic, the four symptoms it produces, and the fix order led by MSS clamping
svg.desc: Top: the arithmetic. An original packet is twenty bytes of IP header, twenty of TCP header and fourteen hundred and sixty of data for fifteen hundred bytes. After IPsec tunnel encapsulation it becomes twenty bytes of new IP, eight of ESP header, sixteen of IV, the whole original fifteen hundred bytes, two of ESP trailer and sixteen of integrity check - about fifteen hundred and sixty-two bytes, which exceeds a fifteen hundred byte MTU and must be fragmented or dropped. Middle: the four symptoms, all with the same signature - small packets pass and large packets are dropped. Ping works but the web page does not open; SSH login succeeds and hangs after a listing; the HTTPS handshake completes and the download sticks at zero percent; and some sites work while others do not because the path MTU differs. Bottom: the fix order with honest verdicts. Lowering the tunnel interface MTU to fourteen hundred is not enough because the host still emits fifteen hundred. Clamping the TCP MSS to thirteen sixty by rewriting the SYN and SYN-ACK is the key measure. Relying on path MTU discovery is unreliable because many firewalls drop the ICMP that carries it. Clearing the DF bit causes fragmentation with poor performance and security devices may still drop the fragments. A final note explains the classic case: the login form is small and the submit payload is not, and the branch router needed to fragment while encapsulation was happening, but PMTUD was broken in the path.
svg.text: "The tunnel is up, ping works, and the application does nothing"
Nearly always MTU. The arithmetic is deterministic, so the diagnosis should be too
THE ARITHMETIC · WHERE THE OVERHEAD COMES FROM

g.text: data 1460 → the whole packet is exactly 1500

svg.text: original packet
encapsulated ≈ 1562 bytes - against a 1500 byte link MTU
THE TWO POSSIBLE OUTCOMES
DF bit set (the normal case)
The router may not fragment. It should send ICMP "fragmentation
needed" back and the sender should shrink - unless a device in
the path eats ICMP, and then the packet simply disappears.
Silent loss of exactly the packets you needed.
SYMPTOM
WHAT IS ACTUALLY HAPPENING
SIGNATURE
ping works, web pages do not open
The TCP handshake is small; the first data segment is not
the classic
SSH login succeeds, then hangs after a large listing
Interactive bytes pass, bulk output does not
same signature
HTTPS handshake fine, download sticks at 0%
Certificate exchange is small, transfer is not
same signature
Some sites work, others never do
Path MTU differs per destination - test path by path
path dependent
MEASURE
EFFECT
IS IT ENOUGH?
ip mtu 1400
the tunnel stops emitting packets larger than 1400
not enough - hosts still send 1500
ip tcp adjust-mss 1360
rewrites MSS in SYN / SYN-ACK so TCP shrinks in advance
the key measure
rely on PMTUD
depends on ICMP "fragmentation needed" reaching the sender
unreliable - firewalls eat ICMP
clear the DF bit
lets routers fragment instead of dropping
poor performance, fragments may be dropped
Case to remember:
the OA login form is a few hundred bytes and the submit payload is several kilobytes. Login worked, submit spun forever - and the fix was clamping MSS, not raising anything.
